tools.name: save-comment
tools.title: Save Comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

tools.name: extract-images
tools.title: Extract Images
tools.description: Extract and fetch images from markdown content. Use this to view screenshots, diagrams, or other images embedded in Linear issues, comments, or documents. Pass the markdown content (e.g., issue description) and receive the images as viewable data.

tools.name: get-issue
tools.title: Get Issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage

tools.name: list-issues
tools.title: List Issues
tools.description: List issues in the user's Linear workspace, including active Triage Intelligence suggestions for issues in triage. For my issues, use "me" as the assignee. Use "null" for no assignee. Filter by status name or type with state; without a team it matches that status in every team.

tools.name: save-issue
tools.title: Save Issue
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `title` and `team` are required. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

tools.name: delete-issue
tools.title: Delete Issue
tools.description: Delete (trash) a Linear issue by ID or identifier. Deleted issues can be restored from the team's Recently deleted issues for 30 days before permanent removal. This is different from closing an issue by moving it to a completed or canceled status.

tools.name: full-text-search-issues
tools.title: Full Text Search Issues

Use list-issues for structured criteria. Supports cursor pagination and returns nextCursor when more results are available.

tools.name: filter-issues

tools.description: Filter Linear issues with a raw GraphQL IssueFilter for criteria list-issues cannot express, such as priority ranges, due-date ranges, estimates, completion dates, or OR conditions. Prefer list-issues for team, status, assignee, label, cycle, project, or priority filters. Supports cursor pagination and returns nextCursor when more results are available.

tools.name: list-comments
tools.title: List Comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for.

tools.name: delete-comment
tools.title: Delete Comment
tools.description: Delete a Linear comment. Inline description comments (those with non-null `quotedText`) anchor a mark in the editor, so their root cannot be deleted — delete the replies individually or resolve the thread instead.

tools.name: read-canvas
tools.title: Read Canvas
tools.description: Read an existing Slack canvas by URL or ID as Markdown and HTML, with a content snapshot and section IDs from a text/type lookup (headings by default). Lookup IDs have no section bodies or offsets; use specific criteria to identify exactly one target before editing.

tools.name: edit-canvas
tools.title: Edit Canvas
tools.description: Apply one confirmed change to an existing Slack canvas after Read Canvas: insert before/after a section, insert at the start/end, replace/delete one section, or rename. Requires the latest snapshot; targeted operations require a section ID and unique lookup text. Whole-canvas replacement is prohibited. Table/rich-section replacement and deletion are refused; Slack has no documented cell/text-range edit API.

tools.description: Lists all channels in the Slack team

tools.name: get-channel-history

tools.name: read-conversation
tools.title: Read Conversation
tools.description: Read messages from a Slack channel, DM, group DM, user DM, or pasted Slack message permalink. When given a U or W user ID, it opens or finds that DM and returns its D-prefixed channel ID; use this to resolve a person before Upload Files. A permalink returns the referenced message and its thread.

tools.name: get-users
tools.title: Get Users
tools.description: List all users in the Slack team

tools.name: find-users
tools.title: Find Users
tools.description: Find Slack users by name, username, display name, or email address. Use this to resolve a person to a user ID. Before uploading files to that person, pass the user ID to Read Conversation and use its returned DM channel ID.

tools.title: Search Messages
tools.description: Search all Messages in the Slack team

tools.name: read-thread
tools.title: Read Thread
tools.description: Read a bounded page of messages in a Slack thread. Use this when the user asks to summarize, inspect, or answer questions about a specific threaded conversation. Requires the channel ID and the parent message timestamp, which can come from Get Channel History or Search Messages. The response includes hasMore and nextCursor so more messages can be fetched when needed.

tools.name: open-group-dm
tools.title: Open Group DM
tools.description: Open or resume a Slack group DM with 2 to 8 users. Use Find Users first to resolve each person to a user ID. Do not include the authenticated user. Returns a group conversation ID that can be passed to Send Message or Upload Files.

tools.name: send-message
tools.title: Send Message
tools.description: Send a Slack message to a channel, group DM, existing DM, or user. Pass a conversation ID or user ID and the message text. When given a user ID, the tool opens or finds the DM first. For messages with file attachments, use Upload Files instead.

tools.name: update-message
tools.title: Update Message
tools.description: Edit a Slack message posted by the authenticated user. Requires the channel ID, message timestamp, and complete replacement text. Use the permalink or a read/search tool to resolve the message first when needed.

tools.name: add-reaction
tools.title: Add Reaction
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction to a Slack message. Requires the channel ID, message timestamp, and Slack emoji name. Use Get Emojis to discover custom workspace emoji names.

tools.name: reply-thread
tools.title: Reply to Thread
tools.description: Post a reply to a Slack thread. Requires the channel ID, the parent message timestamp, and the reply text. Use Read Thread first when context is needed. For replies with file attachments, use Upload Files instead.

tools.name: get-huddle-link
tools.title: Get Huddle Link
tools.description: Get a Slack Huddle join link for a channel, DM, group DM, or user. Pass a conversation ID or user ID. When given a user ID, the tool opens or finds the DM first.

tools.name: upload-files
tools.title: Upload Files
tools.description: Upload one or more local files to a Slack channel, DM, group DM, or thread, optionally with message text. The channel must be a C, D, or G conversation ID; never pass a U or W user ID. For a named person, use Find Users, then Read Conversation, then pass its returned D-prefixed channel ID here. Pass multiple absolute file paths separated by newlines.

tools.name: download-files
tools.title: Download Files
tools.description: Download one or more files (attachments) from Slack to a local folder. Pass Slack file IDs, one per line; file IDs start with F and appear in the `files` array returned by Read Conversation, Read Thread, Get Channel History, or Search Messages. Files are saved to the user's ~/Downloads folder by default, or to an optional destination directory. Returns the saved absolute paths.

tools.name: archive-channels
tools.title: Archive Channels
tools.description: Archive one or more Slack channels. Pass channel IDs (starting with C or G), one per line; use Get Channels to resolve channel names to IDs. Returns whether each channel was archived.

tools.name: rename-channel
tools.title: Rename Channel
tools.description: Rename a Slack channel. Pass the channel ID (starting with C or G) and the new name without the leading #; use Get Channels to resolve channel names to IDs. Names are lowercased and spaces become hyphens. Returns the channel's new name.

tools.description: Add a new to-do in Things. No auth token required. Key params: title, notes, when (today/tomorrow/evening/anytime/someday/YYYY-MM-DD), deadline (YYYY-MM-DD), tags (comma-separated), list-id (project/area ID), checklist-items (newline-separated). Use add-json to add a to-do with headings or nested structure.

tools.name: add-project
tools.title: Add Project
tools.description: Add a new project in Things. No auth token required. Key params: title, notes, when (today/tomorrow/evening/anytime/someday/YYYY-MM-DD), deadline (YYYY-MM-DD), tags (comma-separated), area-id, to-dos (newline-separated to-do titles to add immediately). Use add-json to create a project with headings and nested to-dos in one call.

tools.name: add-json
tools.title: Add Via JSON
tools.description: Add items to Things using the JSON URL scheme. Requires an auth token in preferences. This is the ONLY tool that supports creating projects with headings and nested to-dos in a single call. Tags must be arrays of strings, NOT comma-separated strings.

tools.name: update-todo
tools.title: Update To-Do
tools.description: Update multiple fields of a to-do at once. Requires an auth token in preferences. Key params: title, notes, prepend-notes, append-notes, when (today/tomorrow/evening/anytime/someday/YYYY-MM-DD), deadline (YYYY-MM-DD), tags (replaces all), add-tags (adds without replacing), completed (boolean), canceled (boolean), checklist-items, list-id.

tools.name: update-project
tools.title: Update Project
tools.description: Update a project in Things. Requires an auth token in preferences. Key params: title, notes, prepend-notes, append-notes, when, deadline (YYYY-MM-DD), tags (replaces all), add-tags (adds without replacing), area-id (move to a different area), completed (boolean), canceled (boolean).

tools.name: list-connections
tools.title: List Connections
tools.description: List all saved TablePro database connections with their id, name, type (postgresql, mysql, sqlite, etc.), host, and port. Call this first when the user names a connection so you can pass its id to other tools. Returns an empty list when no connections are saved; throws when the user has not paired the extension with TablePro.

tools.name: list-databases
tools.title: List Databases
tools.description: List database names on a TablePro connection. Use for engines that group objects under a database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MS SQL, ClickHouse). Skip for SQLite, Redis, MongoDB.

tools.name: list-schemas
tools.title: List Schemas
tools.description: List schema names in a database. Use for engines that have schemas inside a database (PostgreSQL, MS SQL, Oracle, Redshift). Pass the database for engines that need it; omit for engines that do not separate database and schema.

tools.name: list-tables
tools.title: List Tables
tools.description: List tables in a connection, optionally scoped to a database or schema. Returns name, schema, database, type (table or view), and approximate row count. Call describe-table next when you need column types.

tools.name: describe-table
tools.title: Describe Table
tools.description: Return the column list, data types, nullability, primary-key flags, defaults, and comments for a table. Always call this before generating queries against a table you have not seen so the SQL matches the real schema. Do not call to list tables (use list-tables) or to get the CREATE TABLE statement (use get-table-ddl).

tools.name: get-table-ddl
tools.title: Get Table DDL
tools.description: Return the CREATE TABLE statement for a table, including indexes and constraints when the engine supports it. Use this when the user asks how a table is defined or wants to copy the structure. Do not call for a column-level overview (use describe-table) or to actually create or modify the table (use run-query, which will route through confirmation).

tools.name: run-query
tools.title: Run Query
tools.description: Execute a SQL query against a connection and return columns and rows. Only read-only statements (SELECT, SHOW, EXPLAIN, DESCRIBE, and WITH clauses that resolve to SELECT) skip confirmation. Every other statement routes through user confirmation; never bypass it and never claim a mutation succeeded before the tool returns. Result rows are capped at 200 by default; pass rowLimit to lower that. The connection's external-access setting can reject the query as read-only; surface that error verbatim. Do not call this tool to inspect schema (use describe-table or get-table-ddl) or to run plans (use explain-query).

tools.name: explain-query
tools.title: Explain Query
tools.description: Wrap a query with EXPLAIN and return the execution plan. Use when the user asks why a query is slow or how the database will run it. Plain EXPLAIN does not execute the underlying query; EXPLAIN ANALYZE on MySQL or PostgreSQL does, and the tool routes that case through user confirmation. Do not call to actually fetch rows (use run-query) or for engines without an EXPLAIN equivalent such as Redis.

tools.name: open-connection-window
tools.title: Open Connection in TablePro
tools.description: Open the TablePro window for a connection so the user can continue interactively. Prefer this over streaming large result sets in chat when the user wants to inspect, edit, or filter data.

tools.name: search-history
tools.title: Search Query History
tools.description: Full-text search the saved TablePro query history. Returns query text, connection id, executed-at timestamp, duration, and row count. Use to find prior work the user is referencing. Do not call to re-run a past query (copy the text into run-query) or to list tables and schemas (use list-tables and list-schemas).

tools.name: get-connection-status
tools.title: Get Connection Status
tools.description: Return the live status of a TablePro connection: connected, connecting, disconnected, or error. Includes current database and schema, server version, and the most recent error message when the connection has failed. Use to answer 'is X up?' style questions before suggesting queries.

tools.name: list-recent-tabs
tools.title: List Recent Tabs
tools.description: List the tabs currently open in TablePro across windows: the connection name, tab type (query, table, structure), display title, and the table or database the tab is scoped to. Use to answer 'what was I just working on?' or to point the user at an existing tab instead of opening a new one.

commands.name: to-base64

commands.name: from-base64

commands.description: Generates an RFC 4122 version 4 compliant Universally Unique Identifier (UUID), also known as a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID). A version 4 UUID relies on random numbers, in this case generated using window.crypto if available and falling back to Math.random if not.

commands.name: generate-qr-code
commands.title: Generate QR Code
commands.description: Generates a Quick Response (QR) code from the input text. A QR code is a type of matrix barcode (or two-dimensional barcode) first designed in 1994 for the automotive industry in Japan. A barcode is a machine-readable optical label that contains information about the item to which it is attached.

commands.name: unescape-string

commands.name: escape-string

commands.name: pseudo

commands.description: A cryptographically-secure pseudo-random number generator (PRNG). This operation uses the browser's built-in crypto.getRandomValues() method if available. If this cannot be found, it falls back to a Fortuna-based PRNG algorithm.

commands.description: Define your own regular expression (regex) to search the input data with, optionally choosing from a list of pre-defined patterns. Supports extended regex syntax including the 'dot matches all' flag, named capture groups, full unicode coverage (including \p{} categories and scripts as well as astral codes) and recursive matching.

commands.name: find-replace

commands.description: Replaces all occurrences of the first string with the second. Includes support for regular expressions (regex), simple strings and extended strings (which support \n, \r, \t, \b, \f and escaped hex bytes using \x notation, e.g. \x00 for a null byte).

commands.name: tail
commands.title: Tail
commands.description: Like the UNIX tail utility. Gets the last n lines. Optionally you can select all lines after line n by entering a negative value for n. The delimiter can be changed so that instead of lines, fields (i.e. commas) are selected instead.

commands.name: head

tools.description: Fetch the full detail of one specific GetNote note by note ID, including content, tags, metadata, attachments, audio/web-page fields, and source URL. Use only when a concrete noteId is known or was returned by another tool. Do not use for search, note counts, quota, or listing recent notes.

tools.name: save-link-note
tools.title: Save Link to GetNote
tools.description: Create a new GetNote link note from a public URL, wait for async processing, and return the generated note. Use when the user asks to save, collect, bookmark, or record a URL. Do not use for plain text notes, quota, search, or modifying existing notes.

tools.name: save-text-note
tools.title: Save Text Note to GetNote
tools.description: Create a new plain-text GetNote note. Use for quick capture, memos, ideas, chat answers, or saving text without a URL. Do not use for link notes, quota, search, deleting notes, or updating an existing note.

tools.name: list-knowledge-bases
tools.title: List GetNote Knowledge Bases
tools.description: List the user's own GetNote knowledge bases/topics with topic IDs and per-knowledge-base note counts. Use only when the user explicitly asks about knowledge bases, topics, topicId, or the count/list of knowledge bases. This is not an API quota tool. Do not use for quota, API usage limits, remaining calls, total account note count, semantic note search, or subscribed read-only knowledge bases.

tools.name: create-knowledge-base
tools.title: Create GetNote Knowledge Base
tools.description: Create a new GetNote knowledge base/topic. Use only when the user explicitly asks to create a knowledge base/topic. Do not use for listing, searching, note counts, quota, or adding notes to an existing knowledge base.

tools.name: list-knowledge-base-notes
tools.title: List GetNote Knowledge Base Notes
tools.description: List notes inside one specific GetNote knowledge base by topicId. Use when the user provides or has selected a topicId and asks to see/list notes in that knowledge base. Do not use for global note search, global note count, API quota, or listing all knowledge bases.

tools.name: search-knowledge-base-notes
tools.title: Search GetNote Knowledge Base Notes
tools.description: Run semantic search within one specific GetNote knowledge base by topicId. Use when the user asks to search/find content inside a named or selected knowledge base/topic. Do not use for global search, total counts, API quota, or listing notes without a search query.

tools.name: add-note-to-knowledge-base
tools.title: Add Note to GetNote Knowledge Base
tools.description: Add one or more existing GetNote notes to one of the user's own writable knowledge bases. Use only when the user explicitly asks to add/move/classify notes into a knowledge base and noteIds plus a topicId are known or can be resolved. Do not use for creating notes, creating knowledge bases, quota, search, or tag changes.

tools.name: add-tags
tools.title: Add Tags to GetNote Note
tools.description: Add manual tags to one specific GetNote note by noteId. Use when the user explicitly asks to tag or add tags for a known note. This adds tags and does not replace all tags. Do not use for knowledge-base classification, note counts, quota, search, or deleting tags.

tools.name: delete-tag
tools.title: Delete GetNote Note Tag
tools.description: Delete one specific tag from one GetNote note by noteId and tagId. Use only when the user explicitly asks to remove/delete a tag. Use get-note-detail first if the tag ID is unknown. Do not use for deleting notes, quota, search, or removing notes from a knowledge base.

tools.name: delete-note
tools.title: Delete GetNote Note
tools.description: Move one specific GetNote note to trash by noteId. Use only when the user explicitly asks to delete/remove/trash a note. Do not use for deleting tags, removing notes from a knowledge base, quota, counts, or search.

Use this to answer questions about portfolio composition, holdings, and asset allocation. This tool takes no arguments — call it with an empty input {}.

tools.title: Get Debt Summary
tools.description: Returns a focused summary of all debt positions including balances, APR, monthly repayments, and repayment status. Use when the user asks about their debts, total debt, or repayment progress. This tool takes no arguments — call it with an empty input {}.

tools.name: get-fire-projection
tools.title: Get FIRE Projection
tools.description: Returns the user's current FIRE baseline: settings, contributions, projection timeline, Coast FIRE analysis, and lump sum solver table. Use ONLY for read-only questions about the current state — 'When will I reach FIRE?', 'What is my FIRE number?', 'Can I coast now?', 'How much to retire 3 years earlier?'. Do NOT use this tool if the user mentions any change, addition, increase, decrease, or hypothetical ('if I add', 'what if', 'if I contributed', 'if growth drops') — use simulate-fire-scenario instead. This tool takes no arguments — call it with an empty input {}.

tools.name: simulate-fire-scenario
tools.title: Simulate FIRE Scenario
tools.description: Runs a custom FIRE projection with overrides and compares it against the user's current baseline. Use this tool whenever the user mentions ANY change or hypothetical — 'if I add £4000/month', 'what if I increase contributions', 'if growth drops to 5%', 'if I invested a lump sum', 'if I retired at 55', 'if I stop contributing at 45'. This tool self-loads the baseline, so you do NOT need to call get-fire-projection first. Available overrides: monthlyContribution (replace total), additionalMonthlyContribution (add to current), currentPortfolioValue, targetValue, annualGrowthRate, annualInflation, withdrawalRate, yearOfBirth, coastFromAge, targetRetirementAge.

tools.name: get-todos
tools.title: Get Todos
tools.description: List, search, and filter the user's Jovida todos. Use this first to read current todos and get their entry_id before updating, completing, or deleting. Defaults to today's pending todos. Works with multilingual queries; preserve the user's language in text fields.

tools.name: view-todo
tools.title: View Todo
tools.description: Get full details for one Jovida todo, recurring todo, or occurrence: description, subtasks with ids/indexes, reminders, reminder channels, and repeat rule. Use before precise subtask edits.

tools.name: create-todo
tools.title: Create Todo
tools.description: Create a single ONE-OFF Jovida todo (cannot repeat). Use for every normal task, including ones with a date, deadline, or reminder/alarm. Resolve relative dates from the user's local timezone/locale and pass either YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetime with offset. For a routine the user explicitly asks to repeat, use Create Recurring Todo instead.

tools.name: create-recurring-todo
tools.title: Create Recurring Todo
tools.description: Create a REPEATING Jovida todo (a routine on a schedule). Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks for repetition like 'every day', 'each Monday', 'weekly', '每天', or '每周一'. Never use for a one-off task that just has a date or a reminder.

tools.name: update-todo
tools.title: Update Todo
tools.description: Change fields of an existing Jovida todo (title, due time, priority, category, description, subtasks, reminders). Only the fields you pass change. For individual subtask check/uncheck/add/remove, use Subtask Todo instead. Get the entry_id from get-todos first — never guess it.

tools.name: subtask-todo
tools.title: Subtask Todo
tools.description: Check, uncheck, add, or remove subtasks without replacing the whole list. Use view-todo first when you need subtask ids or indexes.

tools.name: complete-todo
tools.title: Complete Todo
tools.description: Mark one or more Jovida todos as done. Reversible. Get the entry_id from get-todos first.

tools.name: delete-todo
tools.title: Delete Todo
tools.description: Permanently delete one or more Jovida todos. This is NOT reversible — there is no undo. Prefer complete-todo unless the item was never real. To stop a routine, delete its recurring_id; a single un-materialized occurrence cannot be deleted. Get the entry_id from get-todos first.

tools.name: browse-chats
tools.title: Browse Telegram Chats
tools.description: Browse available Telegram chats (private and group). Returns a list of chats with their IDs, titles, types, and last message info. Use this when you need to find a chat to send a message to or when the user asks to see their chats.

tools.name: read-messages
tools.title: Read Telegram Messages
tools.description: PREFERRED TOOL for reading messages. Use this for all message reading tasks including viewing recent messages, finding what someone said, checking conversation history, or answering questions about message content. Fast and efficient. Only use analyze-messages if you need to inspect images/media attachments. IMPORTANT: Be thorough when searching for information - check BOTH private chats and group chats as the same person may be in multiple conversations. Read enough messages (increase limit if needed) to find all relevant information. When extracting specific details like times, dates, or numbers, quote the EXACT text from the message - do not paraphrase or interpret. Verify information across multiple messages if available.

tools.name: send-message
tools.title: Send Telegram Message
tools.description: Send a message to a specific Telegram chat with optional file attachment from clipboard. Always confirm with the user before sending messages. Use browse-chats tool first to get the chatId. If the user wants to send a file, ask them to copy it to the clipboard first (⌘C on the file in Finder), then set useClipboardFile to true.

tools.name: analyze-messages
tools.title: Analyze Telegram Messages
tools.description: FALLBACK TOOL - Use ONLY when you need to inspect images, photos, or other media attachments in messages. For text-only message reading, always prefer read-messages tool instead. This tool downloads media and uses AI vision to analyze images (e.g., 'What's in this photo?', 'Read text from this image', 'Analyze this receipt'). Requires OpenRouter API key.

tools.title: Open Chat
tools.description: Opens a chat in Beeper by searching for a contact or group name. Use this when the user wants to open, view, or go to a conversation. Supports partial names and fuzzy matching. The 'service' parameter is optional - only specify it if the user explicitly mentions a service like WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, etc.

tools.name: send-message
tools.title: Send Message
tools.description: Sends a message to a contact or group via Beeper. Use this when the user wants to send, text, message, tell, or write to someone. The 'name' parameter is the recipient (supports partial names like 'mom' or 'John'). The 'message' parameter is the text content to send. The 'service' parameter is optional - only include if the user specifies a particular messaging platform.

tools.name: list-accounts
tools.title: List Accounts
tools.description: Lists all connected messaging services in Beeper. Use this when the user asks about their connected accounts, linked services, or wants to see which platforms are available.

tools.name: search-messages
tools.title: Search Messages
tools.description: Searches message content across all Beeper chats. Use this when the user wants to find, search for, or look up specific messages or conversations about a topic. The 'query' parameter is the text to search for. The optional 'sender' parameter can be 'me' (messages sent by user) or 'others' (messages from others). Returns matching messages with sender, service, and timestamps.

tools.name: summarize-unread
tools.title: Summarize Unread Messages
tools.description: Gets unread messages for summarization. Use this when the user wants to know what they missed, summarize unread messages, or catch up on conversations. If 'chatName' is provided, returns unread messages from that specific chat. If 'chatName' is NOT provided, returns a summary list of ALL chats with unread messages (chat names, services, and unread counts). The optional 'service' parameter filters by messaging platform. Summarize the results in a helpful way for the user.

tools.name: summarize-messages
tools.title: Summarize Messages
tools.description: Gets messages from a specific chat for summarization. Use this when the user wants to know what was discussed, asks about recent conversations, or has questions about chat activity like 'what have they been talking about?' or 'any plans mentioned?'. The 'chatName' parameter is the chat name. The optional 'timeRange' parameter specifies whether to get 'today' (default) or 'week' (past 7 days) of messages. The optional 'question' parameter is a specific question to focus on. Returns messages which you should summarize. If no messages are found in the requested time range, it falls back to the most recent day of messages - when 'fallbackToMostRecentDay' is true in the result, mention that you're summarizing the most recent day because there were no messages in the requested time range.
